sections.heading: 21–69: the pattern
sections.html:
• 1 uses et (no hyphen): 21 vingt et un, 31 trente et un, 41 quarante et un, 51, 61.
  • Others use a hyphen: 22 vingt-deux, 35 trente-cinq, 48 quarante-huit, 67 soixante-sept.

sections.heading: 70–99: the tricky part (France and Québec)
sections.html:
French counts by twenties above 60: | Number | Literally | French | |---|---|---| | 70 | 60 + 10 | soixante-dix | | 71 | 60 + 11 | soixante et onze | | 72 | 60 + 12 | soixante-douze | | 77 | 60 + 17 | soixante-dix-sept | | 80 | 4 × 20 | quatre-vingts | | 81 | 4 × 20 + 1 | quatre-vingt-un (no et, no s) | | 85 | | quatre-vingt-cinq | | 90 | 4 × 20 + 10 | quatre-vingt-dix | | 91 | 4 × 20 + 11 | quatre-vingt-onze | | 99 | 4 × 20 + 19 | quatre-vingt-dix-neuf | | 100 | | cent |

Belgium and Switzerland use septante (70), nonante (90), and in Switzerland huitante (80). Canada uses the France system.

Quatre-vingts keeps its s only when nothing follows: quatre-vingts euros, but quatre-vingt-trois.

sections.heading: Pronunciation notes
sections.html:
• six, dix: final x is silent before a consonant (six livres "see"), "z" before a vowel (six‿amis), "s" when alone (j'en ai six "sees").
  • huit: t is silent before a consonant (huit jours "wee joor").
  • cinq: q often silent before a consonant (cinq personnes).
  • neuf → "neuv" before ans and heures: neuf‿ans.
  • vingt: t silent alone, but pronounced in 21–29 (vingt-deux "vant-duh").
  • un/une agrees with a feminine noun: une pomme, vingt et une personnes.
